title: Rubber band around a mug handle
situation: A rubber band is looped around the handle of a mug. You can stretch the band and slide it on the mug, but you cannot cut it or pass it through the ceramic.
object: The object is the loop together with the mug handle acting as an obstacle. The exact roundness of the band is not the issue. What matters is the relationship between the closed loop and the hole through the handle.
allowed_move: The allowed move is a continuous sliding and stretching of the loop while the band stays uncut and never crosses through the handle. The band may get longer, thinner, or uglier; it may not pass through ceramic or open itself.
protected_fact: The protected fact is whether the loop is linked around the handle. That relation survives many changes of shape because the only moves that would remove it are exactly the moves the problem forbids.
course_bridge: This transfers the knot-and-link habit from the course: do not trust the drawing's neatness; ask what relationship cannot be removed by legal deformation. The mug handle plays the role of forbidden matter, and the band plays the role of a loop whose route memory matters.
wrong_transfer: A shallow response says the band looks circular or messy. That talks about geometry of the drawing, not the topological relation that blocks removal. It also misses the illegal move: pulling the band through the handle or cutting it open.
reader_task: Explain whether the band can be freed without cutting it, name the exact move that would be illegal, and say which relationship survives every legal stretch around the handle during the attempt.

title: Two walking routes around a fountain
situation: Two routes across a plaza start and end at the same gates, but one route goes around a fenced fountain and the other does not. The fence is part of the route problem.
object: The object is not the pavement drawing alone. It is the plaza with the fenced region removed and the two paths inside the remaining space. The fence changes the space because it creates a place the path is not allowed to cross.
allowed_move: The allowed move is to slide a route through open walking space while keeping its endpoints at the gates and never crossing the fence. The path may wiggle, shorten, or lengthen, but the endpoints and forbidden region define the same route problem.
protected_fact: The protected fact is whether the route winds around the missing region. A fenced hole can block one path from being changed into the other because any attempted slide would have to cross the fence or move an endpoint.
course_bridge: This is the same first-principles move as loops on surfaces: the missing region changes which deformations are legal. The course habit is to read the obstacle as part of the object, not as decoration in the drawing.
wrong_transfer: A shallow response says both paths are only lines between the same gates. That ignores the obstacle that makes the state space different and treats endpoint agreement as enough by itself.
reader_task: Decide whether one route can be deformed into the other while respecting the fence, say what the fence contributes to the proof, and name the illegal shortcut that would make the routes look equivalent.

title: Matching arrows on a weather map
situation: A small weather map shows wind arrows around a calm point. Nearby arrows turn as you walk around the calm point, and that turning may reveal a local pattern worth counting.
object: The object is the arrow field near an isolated calm point, together with a small loop around that point. The calm point is more than a dot; it is a place where the arrow field fails, and the surrounding arrows are the evidence.
allowed_move: The allowed move is to clean or redraw nearby arrows without removing the calm point from the loop or dragging another calm point inside. The loop must continue to isolate the same failure so the turning account is about one defect.
protected_fact: The protected fact is the total turning of the arrows during one walk around the loop. That turning can survive redrawings even when individual arrows are sketched differently nearby on the map.
course_bridge: This transfers vector-field index from the course: local arrow behavior can become signed evidence without solving the motion everywhere. The everyday map becomes mathematical only after the reader walks around the defect and reads the surrounding arrows.
wrong_transfer: A shallow response tries to predict the full weather. The course idea only needs the local turning account around the defect. It also must not count every calm-looking point unless the point is isolated and has a readable surrounding pattern.
reader_task: Walk around the calm point in words, say what has to stay isolated before an index-like count is meaningful, and state what this local count does not predict about the whole weather system.

title: Moving a sofa through a hallway
situation: A sofa must move from one room to another through a hallway without hitting the walls. The sofa can rotate and slide, but cannot pass through walls or skip a tight turn.
object: The object is the space of all allowed sofa positions and rotations, not merely one drawing of the hallway. One point in that space must record enough information to know where the sofa is and how it is turned.
allowed_move: The allowed move is a continuous path through allowed states where every intermediate position avoids collision. The sofa cannot jump through a tight corner, and the model cannot forget rotation if rotation is part of the physical motion.
protected_fact: The protected fact is whether the start state and end state lie in the same connected region of allowed states. If a wall or narrow turn separates those regions, no continuous legal motion connects the two poses.
course_bridge: This transfers configuration-space modeling: a motion problem becomes a route problem in the space of possible states. The course idea is not to stare harder at the hallway, but to build the right state space and inspect its allowed paths.
wrong_transfer: A shallow response stares only at the floor plan. The proof needs the larger space that records both location and angle. It also has to remove collision states before claiming a route exists.
reader_task: Name what one point of the state space represents, what would count as a forbidden state, and how a path in that space translates back into real sofa motion through the hallway.

title: Stirring coffee in a cup
situation: A spoon stirs coffee inside a round cup, and after the motion every bit of coffee has moved somewhere in the same cup without leaving the filled region of liquid.
object: The object is the filled cup as a disk-like region and the rule sending each starting point to its ending point. The rule, not the stirring story by itself, is what fixed-point thinking inspects.
allowed_move: The allowed move is a continuous self-map of the filled region, with no point sent outside the cup. Nearby starting points must end nearby, and the final positions must still live inside the same filled region.
protected_fact: The protected fact is that a continuous self-map of the right kind of filled region cannot avoid some self-agreement. The conclusion is about at least one starting point matching its ending point, not about all points returning.
course_bridge: This transfers fixed-point thinking: the question is not where the point is, but why some point must return to itself. The everyday motion becomes course mathematics only after the domain, rule, and self-map condition are named.
wrong_transfer: A shallow response says every point returns or that the theorem computes the point. The safe conclusion is existence of at least one fixed point, and only after the self-map contract has been checked.
reader_task: State the domain, the rule, and the exact conclusion without pretending to locate the fixed point or claiming that every bit of coffee returns to its starting place after stirring.

title: Drawing a map on a folded sheet
situation: A map is drawn on a sheet whose opposite edges are taped together according to arrows. After taping, some apparent edges are no longer edges in the finished surface at all.
object: The object is the finished surface created by the taping rule, not the flat sheet before the rule is applied. The arrows and tape are instructions for sameness, so the completed object may have fewer boundaries than the drawing suggests.
allowed_move: The allowed move is to reason after the edge identifications have been made, treating glued points as the same point. Redrawing the sheet is harmless only if the same identification rule is still being used.
protected_fact: The protected fact is the route and boundary behavior of the completed surface after the taped edges are treated as one. A path that looks like it hits an edge on paper may continue through the glued edge in the finished surface.
course_bridge: This transfers quotient-space reading: the drawing is a code, and the gluing rule tells the reader what space the code describes. The course habit is to read the rule before trusting the picture.
wrong_transfer: A shallow response counts the border of the flat sheet as a real boundary after the taping rule has already removed it. That reasons about the code instead of the finished object.
reader_task: Say which points become the same point, what boundary claim changes after the identification, and which feature of the flat drawing no longer deserves to be read literally afterward by the reader.

title: Counting dents on a squeezed ball
situation: A soft ball is squeezed, dented, and redrawn with different patches, but it is never punctured or glued to another piece. The surface stays one closed surface throughout the change.
object: The object is the surface of the ball under legal deformation, not the number of visible dents in one picture. The surface remains the carrier even when its drawing, patching, or local wrinkles change.
allowed_move: The allowed move is to bend and redraw the surface without tearing, puncturing, or changing how the surface is connected. Changing the cell account is allowed only when it still describes the same surface.
protected_fact: The protected fact is a whole-surface count such as Euler characteristic, not the raw count of dents or patch lines. Dents may appear or disappear; the useful count is the one designed to survive legal changes to the surface account.
course_bridge: This transfers the stable-count habit: choose the count designed to survive the legal changes, not the count easiest to see. The everyday squeezed ball becomes a test for separating drawing noise from whole-surface evidence.
wrong_transfer: A shallow response counts every wrinkle as mathematical evidence. Wrinkles are drawing noise unless the argument says why they survive. The repair is to ask which count remains the same after the surface is redrawn honestly.
reader_task: Identify one visible count that is not protected, one whole-surface fact that is protected, and the illegal change that would stop the protected fact from applying to the ball.

title: A robot arm avoiding a blocked zone
situation: A simple arm has two joints and must move from one pose to another while its tip avoids a blocked zone on the table during the entire gradual motion from start to finish.
object: The object is the space of joint choices after forbidden choices have been removed. One point records one complete arm pose, including enough joint data to know where the tip is and whether the pose is allowed.
allowed_move: The allowed move is a continuous path through allowed joint choices, with no intermediate pose entering the blocked zone. The arm may move gradually through joint space, but the path cannot pass through a forbidden pose because the drawing on the table looks convenient.
protected_fact: The protected fact is whether the allowed-pose space has a route from the start pose to the target pose. A blocked zone can create a hole, wall, or disconnected region in the space of choices.
course_bridge: This transfers late-course application thinking: topology studies the shape of possible states before detailed motion equations are solved. The course does not need every control input before it can ask whether the allowed state space has a route.
wrong_transfer: A shallow response draws only the arm in physical space. The topological question lives in the space of all allowed joint choices, after forbidden poses have been removed and real freedoms have been kept.
reader_task: Describe one complete state of the arm, explain what removed states do to the route question, and say what conclusion would overclaim beyond the state-space model itself here in practice.
